milestones.text: spent a whole morning reading up before touching anything
milestones.post: Did the reading. Now the doing. Probably.

milestones.text: bought far more supplies than a beginner could possibly need
milestones.post: In my defence, everything looked useful.

milestones.text: asked a neighbour for advice and got an hour-long lecture, gratefully received
milestones.post: Learned more in an hour over the fence than in a week of guessing.

milestones.text: started a little notebook to keep track of what they were doing
milestones.post: Page one of the notebook. Very official.

milestones.text: made every beginner mistake in the first week, one after another
milestones.post: Collected the full set of beginner mistakes. Onward.

milestones.text: got up early just to check on everything before work
milestones.post: Up before the alarm to check on everything. Who am I.

milestones.text: learned the difference between patience and neglect, the hard way
milestones.post: Turns out 'leave it alone' and 'forget about it' are different things.

milestones.text: lost their first attempt entirely and started again the very next day
milestones.post: Start again. That's the whole trick, apparently.

milestones.text: kept everything going strong through a whole season
milestones.post: A full season and nothing lost. Quietly thrilled.

milestones.text: worked out a weekly routine that actually stuck
milestones.post: Routine found. Weekends sorted.

milestones.text: swapped tips with an old hand at the market and came away with a new trick
milestones.post: Market chat turned into a masterclass.

milestones.text: stopped fussing at every small change and learned to wait and watch
milestones.post: New skill: not fussing. Hardest one yet.

milestones.text: spotted a problem early and sorted it before it spread
milestones.post: Caught it early. Felt like a detective.

milestones.text: filled their first notebook and started a second
milestones.post: Notebook number two. Things are getting serious.

milestones.text: explained the basics to a curious friend without looking anything up
milestones.post: Explained it all to a friend from memory. Progress.

milestones.text: went a whole month without a single disaster
milestones.post: One month, zero disasters. Somebody write it down.

milestones.text: had a week where everything they touched seemed to thrive
milestones.post: Everything's thriving. Not touching anything in case it stops.

milestones.text: planned the whole next season on paper over a winter evening
milestones.post: Next year, mapped out on one sheet of paper. Ambitious.

milestones.text: got asked for advice by someone who had just started
milestones.post: Someone asked ME for advice. Tried to look wise.

milestones.text: rescued something everyone else would have given up on
milestones.post: Brought it back from the brink. Stubbornness pays.

milestones.text: made a simple tool of their own that worked better than the shop-bought one
milestones.post: Made it myself. Works better. Insufferable about it.

milestones.text: kept records for a full year and finally saw the patterns
milestones.post: A year of notes and suddenly it all makes sense.

milestones.text: stopped following the book to the letter and started trusting their own judgement
milestones.post: Ignored the book today. Was right. Don't tell the book.

milestones.text: spent a whole day with a seasoned expert and came home full of plans
milestones.post: One day with an expert, three pages of notes, a head full of plans.

milestones.text: won a ribbon at the local show
milestones.post: A ribbon! A real one. Pinned to the wall already.

milestones.text: gave a short talk to the local society and answered every question
milestones.post: Gave the talk. Survived the questions. Mostly enjoyed it.

milestones.text: spent a season showing a complete beginner the ropes
milestones.post: Showing a newcomer the ropes. Remembering how lost I was.

milestones.text: was trusted with a friend's whole setup for a month away
milestones.post: Minding someone else's pride and joy. No pressure.

milestones.text: had their work admired by an old hand who rarely praises anything
milestones.post: The grumpiest expert I know said 'not bad'. Framing it.

milestones.text: turned last year's failed experiment into a method that works every time
milestones.post: Last year's flop is this year's method.

milestones.text: shared their surplus with the whole street
milestones.post: Too much of a good thing. The neighbours are not complaining.

milestones.text: set up a second spot when the first one ran out of room
milestones.post: Ran out of room. Expanded. No regrets.

milestones.text: took first place at the regional show
milestones.post: First place. I keep checking the card to make sure.

milestones.text: was invited to judge a category at the village show
milestones.post: Judging this year instead of entering. Strange and lovely.

milestones.text: had the local paper print a piece about their work
milestones.post: In the paper! My mother bought five copies.

milestones.text: wrote a little guide for beginners that the local society now hands out
milestones.post: My beginner's guide is now the official one. Wild.

milestones.text: hosted an open day and had a line of visitors at the gate
milestones.post: People queued to see it. Actual people. A queue.

milestones.text: was asked to lead the workshop they once attended as a nervous beginner
milestones.post: Full circle: teaching the class I took on day one.

milestones.text: realised they could not remember the last time something went wrong
milestones.post: Can't remember my last real mistake. Saying that is surely a mistake.

milestones.text: was told by a newcomer that it all started with watching over the fence
milestones.post: Someone started because of me. Best compliment there is.

milestones.text: planted their first row of seeds and checked on it twice before lunch
milestones.post: Seeds in. Watching the soil like it owes me money.

milestones.text: dug their first garden bed, mostly by stubbornness
milestones.post: One bed dug. Earned my supper.

milestones.text: weeded with great enthusiasm and pulled up half the carrots
milestones.post: Weeded with gusto. Removed the carrots. Lesson learned.

milestones.text: pulled their first proper radish and held it up like a trophy
milestones.post: Behold: one radish. Grown by me.

milestones.text: got the tomatoes staked before the first storm, for once
milestones.post: Tomatoes staked in time. Gold star for me.

milestones.text: started a compost heap that actually turned into compost
milestones.post: The compost is composting. Never been prouder of rot.

milestones.text: grew a sunflower taller than the garden fence
milestones.post: Sunflower now taller than the fence. Taller than me, too.

milestones.text: kept the slugs off the lettuces for a whole season
milestones.post: Not a single lettuce lost to slugs. Victory is crunchy.

milestones.text: saved seeds from their own plants for next year
milestones.post: Next year's garden is in these little paper envelopes.

milestones.text: grew enough beans to give bags of them away
milestones.post: Bean surplus. Knock on the door and receive beans.

milestones.text: won second prize for their marrow at the village show
milestones.post: Second-best marrow in the village. I'll take it.

milestones.text: planned and planted a border that flowered from spring to autumn
milestones.post: Something in flower every single month. Planned it that way.

milestones.text: helped a neighbour dig and plan a first vegetable patch
milestones.post: Helped next door start their patch. The garden gang grows.

milestones.text: won best in show for their roses
milestones.post: Best in show. The roses deserve the credit. Mostly.

milestones.text: fed the household from the garden for an entire summer
milestones.post: Haven't bought a vegetable since June.

milestones.text: opened their garden to visitors for the parish open day
milestones.post: Sixty visitors walked through my garden today. Exhausted, glowing.

milestones.text: brought home their first pothos and gave it a name
milestones.post: Meet Gerald. Gerald is a pothos. Gerald must thrive.

milestones.text: drowned their first succulent with kindness and learned what root rot looks like
milestones.post: Farewell, little succulent. Loved too much, too wetly.

milestones.text: downloaded a plant care app and set three watering reminders for one plant
milestones.post: Three reminders, one plant. Taking no chances.

milestones.text: repotted a plant for the first time without wrecking the kitchen
milestones.post: Repotted. Kitchen floor mostly survived.

milestones.text: rooted a cutting in a jar of water and watched the roots appear
milestones.post: Roots! In the jar! A new plant from a bit of old plant.

milestones.text: moved every pot around to find the right light, and it worked
milestones.post: Rearranged the flat around the plants. Worth it.

milestones.text: got their sulky fiddle-leaf fig to put out a new leaf
milestones.post: The fiddle-leaf fig grew a leaf. Notoriously dramatic plant, calm for once.

milestones.text: built a little shelf with grow lights for the darkest corner
milestones.post: Grow light shelf done. The corner now glows purple.

milestones.text: beat a fungus gnat invasion without losing a single pot
milestones.post: Gnats defeated. The plants and I prevail.

milestones.text: identified a friend's mystery plant from the leaves alone
milestones.post: Named the mystery plant at a glance. Plant detective.

milestones.text: got a cutting swap going in the break room at work
milestones.post: Cutting swap at work. Fifteen people came.

milestones.text: coaxed a clearance-shelf orchid into blooming again
milestones.post: The clearance orchid bloomed. Second chances work.

milestones.text: had their plant shelf featured on the local plant shop's online page
milestones.post: My shelf, on the plant shop's page. Famous among ferns.

milestones.text: grew a monstera so big it needed its own corner
milestones.post: The monstera has its own corner now. It pays no rent.

milestones.text: was asked to run a repotting workshop at the plant shop
milestones.post: Taught twelve strangers to repot. Nobody dropped anything.

milestones.text: kept over sixty plants thriving through a whole winter
milestones.post: Sixty-two plants, one winter, zero losses.

milestones.text: bought their first little juniper and stared at it for an hour
milestones.post: First bonsai. Too scared to cut anything.

milestones.text: made their first cut and then spent an evening checking it was the right one
milestones.post: First snip. Then a long, careful read. It was fine.

milestones.text: went along to a beginners' evening at the bonsai club
milestones.post: First club night. Everyone whispers around the trees.

milestones.text: wired a branch for the first time without snapping it
milestones.post: Wired a branch. It bent, it didn't snap. Breathing again.

milestones.text: kept their juniper happy through its first winter
milestones.post: Survived the winter together, me and the juniper.

milestones.text: moved their tree into a proper shallow bonsai pot
milestones.post: New pot. The tree looks suddenly serious.

milestones.text: pinched back the new growth at exactly the right time, for once
milestones.post: Timed the pinching perfectly. The tree seems pleased.

milestones.text: styled a cheap nursery shrub into something that looked like a tiny old tree
milestones.post: Bought a shrub, made a tree. Feels like magic.

milestones.text: learned to tell when a tree needs water just by the weight of the pot
milestones.post: I can tell it's thirsty by lifting it now. Weird skill.

milestones.text: started a maple from seed with a ten-year plan
milestones.post: A maple seedling and a plan for 2036. Patience is the hobby.

milestones.text: showed a tree at the club's spring exhibition
milestones.post: My little juniper, on a real display table.

milestones.text: talked a newer member through wiring a first branch
milestones.post: Helped someone wire their first branch. Their hands shook. Mine did too, once.

milestones.text: got a compliment on their tree's roots from the club's oldest member
milestones.post: The club's oldest member liked my roots. Floating.

milestones.text: won best tree in show at the regional bonsai exhibition
milestones.post: Best in show. Six years of tiny decisions.

milestones.text: gave a live styling demonstration at the club
milestones.post: Did a live styling demo. The tree cooperated, thankfully.

milestones.text: watched a tree they grew from a cutting finally look truly ancient
milestones.post: Seven years from a twig. It looks centuries old now.

milestones.text: watched their first hive inspection with their heart in their throat
milestones.post: First inspection. Ten thousand bees and one very still person.

milestones.text: built their first hive box, slightly crooked
milestones.post: Hive box built. It leans a little. The bees don't mind.

milestones.text: learned to move slowly and calmly around the hive
milestones.post: Slow hands, calm breath. Bees like it, I like it.

milestones.text: tasted honey straight from the comb at their mentor's hive
milestones.post: Honey from the comb. Now I understand why people do this.

milestones.text: spotted the queen on their own for the first time
milestones.post: Found the queen! Long body, total confidence.

milestones.text: got their colony through its first winter
milestones.post: They made it through the winter. Buzzing in the spring sun.

milestones.text: lit the smoker on the first try and kept it going the whole inspection
milestones.post: Smoker lit first time. Small victories, cool smoke.

milestones.text: took off their first jars of honey
milestones.post: Our own honey. Tastes like the whole summer.

milestones.text: caught a swarm from a neighbour's hedge in a basket
milestones.post: Caught a swarm in a basket. The neighbour cheered from a safe distance.

milestones.text: learned to tell a calm hive from an unsettled one by the sound alone
milestones.post: I can hear when they're happy now. Hard to explain.

milestones.text: split a strong colony into two thriving hives
milestones.post: One hive is now two. Bee real estate expanding.

milestones.text: sold honey at the market and ran out by noon
milestones.post: Sold out by noon. Should have brought more jars.

milestones.text: showed a nervous friend inside a hive without a single flinch
milestones.post: Opened the hive for a friend. They stayed calm, so did I.

milestones.text: won first prize for their honey at the county show
milestones.post: First prize honey. The bees did the work, I did the jars.

milestones.text: kept six colonies strong through a hard winter
milestones.post: Six hives, one long winter, all alive. Proud beekeeper.

milestones.text: became the one neighbours call to collect swarms all season
milestones.post: Swarm call number nine this year. I am the bee person now.

milestones.text: planted a first bed of thyme, sage and mint by the kitchen door
milestones.post: Thyme, sage and mint by the door. A start.

milestones.text: learned to tell chamomile from mayweed, eventually
milestones.post: Chamomile, not mayweed. Probably. Fairly sure.

milestones.text: hung their first bundles of herbs to dry from the rafters
milestones.post: Bundles drying from the rafters. The house smells wonderful.

milestones.text: kept the mint from swallowing the whole bed
milestones.post: The mint has been contained. For now.

milestones.text: brewed a chamomile tea from flowers they grew themselves
milestones.post: Tea from my own chamomile. Tastes like a quiet evening.

milestones.text: started a book of pressed leaves with notes beside each one
milestones.post: Pressed my first leaves into the herb book. Very scholarly.

milestones.text: swapped seeds with a traveller at the market
milestones.post: Traded seeds with a stranger. New herbs to try.

milestones.text: grew a whole bed of lavender and sold bundles to the neighbours
milestones.post: Lavender bundles all round. The lane smells lovely.

milestones.text: laid out a proper knot of beds, each herb in its place
milestones.post: Every herb has a home now. Neat little rows.

milestones.text: made a batch of lavender soap from their own flowers
milestones.post: Lavender soap, from flower to bar. Smells like June.

milestones.text: was asked by the cook at the big house to supply herbs every week
milestones.post: The big house wants my herbs every week. Honoured.

milestones.text: taught the neighbours' children to name every herb in the bed
milestones.post: The children can name all twelve herbs now. Proud teacher.

milestones.text: dried and labelled a whole season's harvest in neat jars
milestones.post: Forty jars, all labelled. The pantry looks like an apothecary.

milestones.text: had cuttings from their garden asked for by people from the next village
milestones.post: Visitors from two villages over, asking for cuttings.

milestones.text: won the herb prize at the harvest fair
milestones.post: Best herbs at the harvest fair. The rosemary is delighted.

milestones.text: kept a herb garden so fine that the local apothecary came to study it
milestones.post: The apothecary took notes in MY garden today.

milestones.text: kept a first row of seedlings alive to harvest
milestones.post: They lived! All of them!

milestones.text: learned which weeds to pull and which to leave
milestones.post: Weed or not weed. I know now.

milestones.text: dug a new bed by hand
milestones.post: New bed, dug by hand.

milestones.text: grew something from seed and ate it
milestones.post: Seed to plate.

milestones.text: learned when to plant by watching the weather
milestones.post: Watching the sky now.

milestones.text: kept the garden going through a dry spell
milestones.post: Watered through the dry spell.

milestones.text: saved seed from a favourite plant
milestones.post: Saving seed for next year.

milestones.text: had the first flowers of the year in the house
milestones.post: First flowers on the table.

milestones.text: learned to tell when a crop is ready by touch
milestones.post: Ready by feel.

milestones.text: grew plenty to share along the street
milestones.post: Plenty to share.

milestones.text: planted a new bed laid out to a plan of their own
milestones.post: My own plan, planted.

milestones.text: got a fussy plant to flower at last
milestones.post: It flowered! Finally!

milestones.text: had passers-by stop to admire the garden
milestones.post: People stop to look now.

milestones.text: grew a whole bed of herbs for the kitchen
milestones.post: Herbs for days.

milestones.text: won a prize for a vegetable at the fair
milestones.post: Prize vegetable. Ribbon pinned up.

milestones.text: grew enough to keep the kitchen supplied all summer
milestones.post: Didn't buy greens all summer.

milestones.text: was asked for advice by a neighbour starting out
milestones.post: Advice-giver now.

milestones.text: brought a neglected plot back to life
milestones.post: Neglected plot, back to life.

milestones.text: had the garden opened for visitors
milestones.post: Garden open to visitors!

milestones.text: grew a rare plant others had given up on
milestones.post: The rare one thrives here.

milestones.text: won best garden in town
milestones.post: Best garden in town!

milestones.text: became the one the whole street asks about plants
milestones.post: The street's plant person.

milestones.text: opened the hive for the first time without fuss
milestones.post: First look inside. Calm.

milestones.text: learned to move slowly around the bees
milestones.post: Slow and calm. The bees like that.

milestones.text: took a first small harvest of honey
milestones.post: First honey. Sticky everything.

milestones.text: spotted the queen without help
milestones.post: Found the queen myself.

milestones.text: caught a swarm and settled it in a new hive
milestones.post: Caught a swarm!

milestones.text: got the bees through a hard winter
milestones.post: Every hive made it through.

milestones.text: sold honey at the market
milestones.post: Honey for sale.

milestones.text: had enough honey to give a jar to everyone at the table
milestones.post: Honey for everyone.

milestones.text: kept a whole row of thriving hives
milestones.post: A row of hives, all humming.

milestones.text: was called in to help with a neighbour's swarm
milestones.post: Called in for a swarm.

sessions.text: Pottered about for longer than they meant to.
Wrote a few notes in their little book afterwards.
Found the whole thing quietly calming.
Spent a while just watching, which counts too.
Did the small jobs nobody else would notice.
Lost track of time in the best way.
Made a mental list of what to do next time.
Came back inside with soil under their fingernails.
Pulled weeds until the bed looked tidy again.
Watered everything in the cool of the morning.
Planted out a few seedlings before the sun got high.
Turned every pot a quarter turn toward the light.
Checked the soil of every pot with a fingertip.
Wiped the dust off the big leaves, one by one.
Trimmed a few shoots, then sat back to look for a long while.
Watched the bees come and go from the entrance for a while.
Moved slowly and kept everything calm.
Cut a handful of sprigs for the kitchen.
Tied up a few bundles to dry.
